title: TLS handshake timeout when using docker pull
body:
### Description

Versions 28.0.2 up to 28.1.1 of docker produce the following error when using `docker pull hello-world` : `Error response from daemon: Get "https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/": net/http: TLS handshake timeout`. Going back to version 28.0.1 solves the issue.

Sometimes, there are other intermittent error messages, but it always ends up settling on the `TLS handshake timeout` one afterwards. Here are two different errors I've seen intermittently:

* `docker: Error response from daemon: Get "https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/": net/http: request canceled while waiting for connection (Client.Timeout exceeded while awaiting headers)`
* `Error response from daemon: Get "https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/": context deadline exceeded`

### Reproduce

1. `sudo apt install --allow-downgrades -y docker-ce=5:28.0.1-1~ubuntu.24.04~noble docker-compose-plugin=2.33.1-1~ubuntu.24.04~noble docker-buildx-plugin=0.21.1-1~ubuntu.24.04~noble docker-ce-cli=5:28.0.1-1~ubuntu.24.04~noble docker-ce-rootless-extras=5:28.0.1-1~ubuntu.24.04~noble`
2. `docker pull ubuntu:noble`
3. Success
4. `sudo apt install --allow-downgrades -y docker-ce=5:28.1.1-1~ubuntu.24.04~noble docker-compose-plugin=2.35.1-1~ubuntu.24.04~noble docker-buildx-plugin=0.23.0-1~ubuntu.24.04~noble docker-ce-cli=5:28.1.1-1~ubuntu.24.04~noble docker-ce-rootless-extras=5:28.1.1-1~ubuntu.24.04~noble`
5. `docker pull ubuntu:noble`
6. Error response from daemon: Get "https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/": net/http: TLS handshake timeout

### Expected behavior

Pull of public libraries should always succeed in the absence of any network issues.

comments.author: participant1
comments.body: @participant2 any chance this could be related to networking changes in v28?

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
As discussed offline - I can't see anything in 28.0.2 that could cause this ... there was a lot of change to container networking in 28.0.0 (with fixes in 28.0.1), but nothing that should affect the daemon's communication with the registry, from the host rather than a container.

There was some refactoring of registry code in 28.0.2, maybe that's related. Image pulls aren't broken in-general, so I guess we're looking for something related to the specific environment or config.

It seems that the initial ssl handshake is broken down into three packets, the first is correctly acknowledged, the second isn't, and the third is only sent after a 10s timeout. comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
By looking at the `.golangci.yml` file at the root of moby/moby, it seems the golang versions for various Docker versions are the following:
* Docker 28.0.1 used golang 1.23.6
* Docker 28.0.2 used golang 1.23.7 and introduced the issue
* Docker 28.1.1 used golang 1.23.8 and still had the issue
* Docker 28.2 used golang 1.24.3 and solved the issue

The same issue started plaguing me on another project over here:
* [hashicorp/packer-plugin-amazon 1.3.6 used golang 1.21.0](https://github.com/hashicorp/packer-plugin-amazon/blob/dd670e565586b9ee18295441d9c713c6842c6976/go.mod#L3)
* [hashicorp/packer-plugin-amazon 1.3.7 used golang 1.23.6 and toolchain go1.23.9](https://github.com/hashicorp/packer-plugin-amazon/blob/61682d433559c10f0404ae820aa4686356262b4b/go.mod#L3-L5) and introduced the issue

According to the golang [1.23.7 changelog](https://go.dev/doc/devel/release#go1.23.0) : « go1.23.7 (released 2025-03-04) includes security fixes to the net/http package ». Releases 1.23.8, 1.23.10, 1.24.0, 1.24.1 and 1.24.2 all include release notes that mention « security fixes to the net/http package ».

I looked into the changelogs and the issues closed with each of these golang releases. I found these CVEs that were addressed in the net/http package :
* https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-22870 (fixed in golang 1.24.1, backported in 1.23.7)
* https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-22871 (fixed in golang 1.24.2, backported in 1.23.8)
* https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2025-4673 (fixed in golang 1.24.4, not backported)

The issue for the last CVE seemed relevant because of the symptom being a TLS Handshake Timeout: https://github.com/golang/go/issues/73118.

- Docker 28.0.1 used golang 1.22.0; golang.org/x/net v0.33.0; golang.org/x/crypto v0.31.0
- Docker 28.0.2 used golang 1.23.0; golang.org/x/net v0.36.0; golang.org/x/crypto v0.35.0
- Docker 28.1.1 used golang 1.23.0; golang.org/x/net v0.39.0; golang.org/x/crypto v0.37.0
- Docker 28.2.0 used golang 1.23.0; golang.org/x/net v0.39.0; golang.org/x/crypto v0.37.0

If, instead, I rely on `moby/Dockerfile`, I get this result:
- Docker 28.0.1 used golang 1.23.6
- Docker 28.0.2 used golang 1.23.7
- Docker 28.1.1 used golang 1.23.8
- Docker 28.2.0 used golang 1.24.3

I can't make more sense of this data. The 1.23.6 version I see in hashicorp's packer-plugin-amazon is confusing because that specific version worked in Docker 28.0.1. But then again there's the 1.23.9 toolchain that might be superseding?

Maybe you can make more sense of this data than I can!

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I have just realized I have been having a similar issue with https://github.com/hashicorp/terraform for a while now. It is similar because it also leads to net/http: TLS handshake timeout issues. But unlike with this current issue, an automatic retry mechanism often ends up successfully connecting at some point during its maximum 5 attempts. The speed was degraded though.

The latest release is based on golang 1.24.2 which includes commits that were backported to 1.23.7 and 1.23.8. So I bumped Terraform's golang version to 1.24.4 and built from source. I didn't touch any of the library versions ~and this new binary is free of issues~. I had a lucky streak I guess, but the problem was still there after bumping the golang version. I then bumped both the net package from v0.38.0 to v0.39.0 and crypto from v0.36.0 to v0.37.0, and so far so good.

Just in case you're not familiar with the docker pull workflow, the daemon first needs to get a token from `auth.docker.io` even for public images, so that looks normal to me.

Here's a simple python code that I was using to test the connection on devices to distinguish if the issue is related to docker daemon or something else.

``` Python
import urllib.request
import json
# Get auth token
url = "https://auth.docker.io/token?scope=repository:library/hello-world:pull&service=registry.docker.io"
response = urllib.request.urlopen(url, timeout=10)
print(f"Status: {response.status}")
token = json.loads(response.read())["token"]
# Get manifest
url = "https://registry-1.docker.io/v2/library/hello-world/manifests/latest"
req = urllib.request.Request(url, headers={"Authorization": f"Bearer {token}"})
response = urllib.request.urlopen(req, timeout=10)
print(f"Status: {response.status}")

```
